# Agent Taskbay

Agent Taskbay is a self-hosted console for people who work with A2A agents. It stores tasks in its own database, shows them after the browser closes, and asks a person when an agent needs input or an approval. It does not run agents.

Created and maintained by Shashi Kanth G S, part of Allsrc. MIT license. Version 1.0.0 is published on npm as `agent-taskbay`. Experimental features, including this repository's extensions, are called out in the docs and can change in any minor release.

## Quickstart

Node.js 22.19 or newer.

```bash
npx agent-taskbay
```

The console listens on `http://127.0.0.1:3002` and uses an embedded database in `~/.agent-taskbay`. Local mode signs you in as an administrator and binds to loopback.

```bash
npx agent-taskbay demo-agent
```

Sample agents listen on port 4010. The cards are:

- `http://127.0.0.1:4010/showcase/card.json` — form, A2UI surface, and approval request
- `http://127.0.0.1:4010/form/card.json` — structured form
- `http://127.0.0.1:4010/approver/card.json` — approval request
- `http://127.0.0.1:4010/a2ui/card.json` — A2UI confirmation surface
- `http://127.0.0.1:4010/automation/card.json` — tasks another system already started

Connect one from **Agents → Add agent**. These are fixtures, not product agents.

## What it is

- An A2A client with a database and a web console. The browser never talks to agents and never sees their credentials.
- Commands are saved before they are sent. Workers follow tasks by stream, push callback, and polling.
- Local mode uses PGlite. A shared deployment uses PostgreSQL, OIDC, and separate worker processes.
- The application does not send telemetry. Local mode creates no account.
- Content the console shows: text, Markdown, JSON, CSV, and archived images, audio, video, and PDF. Agent-supplied code is not run. Remote media URLs are not loaded.
- The audit trail is append-only, enforced by database triggers. That is immutability in the database, not cryptographic tamper evidence. See the glossary and the threat model.
- The optional notification webhook is HMAC-signed. An approval decision is not a signature. It is bound to a SHA-256 digest of the action that was sent.

## Agent Card

Give the console the card URL. A URL that ends in `.json` is fetched as given. Any other URL is resolved at `/.well-known/agent-card.json`.

Extensions are objects, not bare strings. These two URIs are defined by this project. They are not A2A standards.

```json
{
  "name": "Database migration agent",
  "description": "Asks a person before it applies a migration.",
  "version": "1.0.0",
  "supportedInterfaces": [
    { "url": "http://127.0.0.1:5050/a2a", "protocolBinding": "JSONRPC", "protocolVersion": "1.0" }
  ],
  "capabilities": {
    "streaming": false,
    "pushNotifications": false,
    "extensions": [
      { "uri": "https://extensions.allsrc.dev/agent-taskbay/approval-request/v1", "required": false },
      { "uri": "https://extensions.allsrc.dev/agent-taskbay/structured-form/v1", "required": false }
    ]
  },
  "defaultInputModes": ["text/plain"],
  "defaultOutputModes": ["text/plain"],
  "skills": [
    { "id": "migrate", "name": "Migrate", "description": "Propose a schema migration." }
  ]
}
```

## Task states

A2A states include `submitted`, `working`, `input-required`, `auth-required`, `completed`, `failed`, `canceled`, and `rejected`. On the wire they are `TASK_STATE_*`.

`auth-required` means the agent needs credentials. It is not a human approval. Taskbay shows it and asks the person to authorize elsewhere, then reply. There is no guided handoff.

An approval is `input-required` (`TASK_STATE_INPUT_REQUIRED`) plus one data part:

```json
{
  "data": {
    "title": "Delete the staging cluster",
    "summary": "Removes all staging nodes and volumes.",
    "risk": "high",
    "expiresInSeconds": 3600,
    "action": { "kind": "send_message", "text": "Approved. Delete the staging cluster." }
  },
  "mediaType": "application/vnd.agent-taskbay.approval-request+json"
}
```

`risk` is `low`, `medium`, or `high`. `action.kind` is `send_message` or `send_data`. A text part, or fields such as `riskLevel` and `description`, does not open a decision. The agent must advertise the extension URI. The part has to be on the latest input-required status message.

Approving sends that action once, on the same task. The message's `metadata.approval` is:

```json
{
  "requestId": "<uuid>",
  "decisionId": "<uuid>",
  "revision": 1,
  "revisionDigest": "<sha-256 hex of the approved action>"
}
```

Rejecting or asking for changes sends nothing. The digest covers the canonical JSON of the action, with object keys sorted at every level. It is not a signature. A chat reply can still be sent while an approval is open.

## Where it fits

| You need | What fits |
| --- | --- |
| One place to start, follow, and approve work on A2A agents you already run | Agent Taskbay |
| The framework's own pause (LangGraph `interrupt()` with a checkpointer, an ADK confirmation, CrewAI human input) | That framework. This repository does not bridge those pauses. The ADK gap is issue 18. |
| A stable HTTP API or a client library for the console | Not this project today (issue 31). |
| Proof the agent performed the approved action, or a cryptographic audit log | Not claimed. |

Any agent that publishes an A2A 1.0 card works as a plain chat target. A 0.3 card is accepted through the gateway's legacy path and is not verified against real 0.3 agents. Other frameworks need an A2A interface. There is no AutoGen example.

## Python helper

`sdk/python` is an experimental helper that serves an agent and sends the approval part above. It is not the client SDK. It is not on PyPI.

```bash
pip install "git+https://github.com/allsrc/agent-taskbay.git#subdirectory=sdk/python"
```

From a checkout: `pip install -e sdk/python`. `examples/python-requests-taskbay` is a small agent built with it. The LangGraph, CrewAI, and Google ADK directories under `examples/` are sketches and do not open a connection.

## Limits that are easy to miss

- No independent security review.
- No stable console API, no service tokens, no `/api/v1`.
- Local mode is not a security boundary.
- No container image, Compose file, or Helm chart.
- No gRPC. The AG-UI adapter is experimental and off by default.
- Tested in CI on Node.js 22.19 and PostgreSQL 18 on Linux.
